stem.text: Which features of monoclonal antibodies make them useful in the diagnosis and treatment of disease?

items: A particular monoclonal antibody attaches to a specific antigen.
Identical monoclonal antibodies can be produced in large numbers.
Binding a monoclonal antibody to its specific antigen may mark that antigen for destruction by white blood cells.
Fluorescent or radioactive markers can be attached to a monoclonal antibody to show where the antigen is in the body.
